shared_elements: horizontal band of closely repeated vertical elements (fluted headdress in A; hatched band in B)
rows of small repeated motifs across a surface
curved hook-like forms (curls in A; beaks/limbs in B)
justification: Both are stone reliefs featuring profile-viewed heads beneath a horizontal register of tightly repeated vertical strokes, and both use rows of small repeated motifs to fill a field. But A is a single, highly finished naturalistic human head with meticulously drilled spiral curls and a polished surface, while B is a coarse, schematic pillar crowded with abstracted animals and arms in shallow, flat-cut relief — the manner of carving and the subject matter have essentially nothing in common.
